name: Abishur
title: Descendant of Judah in the line of Hezron
summary: In the genealogy of 1 Chronicles, Abishur appears as part of the tribe of Judah, belonging to the further lineage of Hezron. He was the son of Shammai and had Abinadab as a brother. Through his marriage to Abihail, he became the father of Ahban and Molid. Although Abishur belongs to a side branch and not the direct messianic line of David, his place in the genealogy testifies to the thorough preservation of Judah's family history – a witness to God's faithfulness to the entire tribe, not just the royal line.
roles: Ancestor in the lineage of Judah

keyEvents.title: Place in the genealogy of Judah
keyEvents.description: Abishur is listed in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah as the son of Shammai and brother of Abinadab, in a side line of Hezron's descendants.

keyEvents.title: Marriage with Abihail and Descendants
keyEvents.description: Abishur married Abihail, and they had two sons: Akban and Molid. These continued the lineage within the tribe of Judah.

versions.reason: [minor] The summary is very similar to the previous version (version 1). It should be rephrased more to avoid repetition and provide fresh text.; [major] Abishur belongs to Hezron's line in the tribe of Judah. Hezron was a grandson of Judah, but the genealogy places Abishur several generations after the patriarchs. Given that Shammai is a descendant in a side line extending beyond the patriarchal period, 'patriarchs' may be imprecise. However, it is very difficult to date Abishur accurately – he may have lived around the time of the judges or the united kingdom. Without secure dating, 'judges' or 'united-kingdom' is more likely than 'patriarchs', but the uncertainty is great. 'judges' is a reasonable choice given the generational distance from Judah.; [minor] The role 'ancestor in Judah's line' is correct, but could be supplemented with something like 'father of Akban and Molid' to make it more specific.; [minor] The two key events cover the material well, but they overlap somewhat. The descriptions can be made more distinct.

footnotes.text: The name Abishur (Hebrew: אֲבִישׁוּר, 'Avishur) is a compound name from 'avi' (my father) and 'shur' (wall). It likely means "my father is a wall" or "father of protection", suggesting the family's role as guardians and source of security.

The genealogies in 1 Chronicles chapter 2 were probably compiled during the Persian period, after the Babylonian exile, to restore tribal identity, inheritance rights, and connection to the land. Such lists had practical importance for property distribution and cultic service.

Hezron's line is of special theological significance because it leads to King David and the messianic line. Abishur represents a side branch of this family, showing the breadth of Judah's tribal genealogy.
The name Abihail (Hebrew: אֲבִיחָיִל) means "my father is strength" or "father of power". It is a common biblical name borne by several people in the Old Testament, both men and women.
